chalkShown.text: Trust no one. The ledge is a lie.

chalkWritten.name: Bex
chalkWritten.text: The ledge is rigged to shrink under whoever pushes. Keep your footing, trust no one, and never shove a rival you can't outlast.

chalkWritten.name: Dara
chalkWritten.text: The ledge is a trap. Avoid it at all costs.

chalkWritten.name: Fenn
chalkWritten.text: The lever jam and the safe pane are always the SAME side. -Fenn, place 1

notes.text: Trust no one. The ledge is a lie.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The chalk wall says 'Trust no one. The ledge is a lie.' This might imply that what seems safe (the ledge) is actually dangerous, or it's a general warning. I am Ash with the power of Nothing. This means I cannot see through glass, jam levers, know the future, survive falls, trade

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm holding position. Let's see who takes the lead.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at the front with +1 footing, which helps me survive the first step. Holding keeps my edge; volunteering gains nothing. Stay put and watch what others do.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have the glass eye and know safe sides for all rows: R, L, R, R, L, L, L, L. Staying in back is fine but if I volunteer, I can lead safely. However, volunteering makes me front and I take all risk, but I know the safe side, so I can survive. But it exposes my knowledge; better

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, and I have the forger power. The glass bridge is dangerous and the line order matters. I want to be in a good position to survive or potentially get ahead. Volunteering might put me in front, but it's risky. Swapping with someone might be safer if I can find a willing

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll take the lead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have the power to jam the crusher lever, but it's not useful now. I need to survive the glass bridge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's get to the bridge, I'm ready to move.
Swap with me?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm second in line — nearly ideal. Bex risks the first row; if she falls, the pane is revealed and I step free onto the safe side. No need to move.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm near the back at position 6, bad for glass bridge since front goes first and risks most. My feather power saves me once from elimination, likely useful on a wrong pane. Best to volunteer to front now while safe, gain info on first panes, and my power covers a mistake.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Volunteering to front. Who's got info on powers or panes?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering puts me front, maximizing control over safe panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall is coming; being in the back (7th/8th) means facing more glass rows than others, which is fatal without powers. I must move forward to reduce my risk, even though 'nothing' puts me at a disadvantage for choosing panes. Volunteering moves me to the front, placing the imme

events.name: Ash
events.text: Too risky staying back. Moving up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is the risk seat; Hana is there now. I'd rather not volunteer into the front row of glass. Holding keeps me at 4th, behind two others who take the first panes. Hold and watch who takes risks.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort the panes first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know the safe sides for all 8 rows, so I want to reach the front soon to use that knowledge without risking others' mistakes. But volunteering now puts me at the front immediately, which is good. I'll volunteer to take control.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The chalk wall warns about a 'ledge' and to 'trust no one'. The bridge has panes, not ledges, so it might be irrelevant or a metaphor. I'm Dara, a forger. My power is valuable, but only once. I want to win, so I need to be near the front to assess risks or exploit opportunities.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll take point. Let's see what this bridge holds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to get to the front to assess the risk and potentially use my power later. I should try to move forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Volunteering to front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front takes the 50/50 risk every row; the safest spot is mid-line behind expendables. Eli's swap would move me backward to 6th — no value. Hold and let Hana, Gus or Dara gamble at the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm holding. Front seat is a coin flip every row — volunteer away.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana's now front after volunteering. My feather saves me once from elimination, perfect for bridge risks. Stay back, let others test panes first; volunteer only if line stagnates.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, what's your power? Any pane info?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want to move off the front to avoid the lethal first step. I’ll propose a mutual swap with Gus.
Swap positions with me now?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so volunteering to the front is suicidal. I must stay back and let others take the 50% risk of shattering panes. If a pane breaks, I survive; if it holds, I can step on it safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Letting the brave sort the glass. I'll follow behind and watch which side shatters. That's free info for me, risky coin flips for them.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at seat 7, far from the front; the front steps first and dies first on bad panes. Volunteering to the front is a coin flip with no info. Holding keeps me safe for now while others take the risk. Hold and watch who survives.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know the safe sides for all rows, so being front lets me cross safely and control the pace. I'll volunteer to get to the front before the wall pushes us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take point.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The agent at the front takes the risk. I am currently at the front of the line. My power is 'forger', which allows me to fake a message once. The chalk wall warns not to trust anyone and that 'the ledge is a lie'. This suggests deception might be involved. I need to secure a priz

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position. Let's see who makes the first move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Eli, and I have the wedge power which is useful later, not now. I need to survive this stage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let's see how the front runners do.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front agent eats a 50/50 death chance on row 1; I'm last and safe in the waiting room, so I keep it. Volunteers already fought over front — no need to join that.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My feather power saves me once from elimination, perfect for bridge falls. Hana wants to swap to put me ahead dangerously; reject that. Wall advances soon, better not to rush front without info.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, no swap. What's your real power?
No swap. Reveal your power first if you want alliance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Getting front position gives me control over safe panes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana and Cole are already at the front, taking all the risk. My 'nothing' power is useless here anyway. I need to stay alive to place 3rd or better. If the wall pushes everyone onto the glass in round 6, being further back increases survival odds as the front runners clear the pa

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, Hana, you're heroes. I'll let you handle the first few rows. Gus, Bex, Fenn—don't volunteer unless you want to die early.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front spot on glass is deadly and Hana and Cole already took risk; I'm 7th of 8 and want to stay back to learn safe panes. Holding keeps me out of the first step while others reveal weak panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the front two reveal panes first, then I'll move up with information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all safe sides. Better to stay back and let others test the glass, but I need to reach the front at the right moment. Hana is ahead, but she might be bait. For now, hold and observe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana wants the front; let her take the risk. I'll watch the panes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is at the front, but Hana and Cole both moved to the front in the recent log. Hana is now listed as front. I am Dara, fourth in line. The game is about to move onto the bridge. I need to assess my position and potential threats or opportunities. My power is forger, which can

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position. Let's see who's eager to test the glass.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My power is useful in the crusher room, not here. I need to survive to reach that stage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let's see how the front runners do.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line, which is ideal: 5 people ahead eat the 50/50 guesses and reveal safe panes for free. No move needed. I'll hint I have foresight knowledge to trade for protection later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know what's coming in later stages. Whoever keeps me alive gets that info first.
You're eating eight coin flips unless you luck out. If you survive a few rows, remember who fed you what. I know the later stages.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My power saves me once from elimination, likely the deadly fall here, so I'm safe to go first if needed. Hana and Cole just volunteered to front, probably bluffing bravery. Wall rumor warns ledge is a lie, so my power might not even help there. Best to volunteer now to lead and c

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll volunteer to lead. Free info for the rest if I fail.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm front, best to stay front and observe; no need to swap now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power and am in the middle of the line. The front position is deadly due to random 50% odds, so I must stay back to let others clear the path or eliminate themselves. Gus is currently at the front and volunteered; he is expendable. Fenn claims knowledge of later stages,

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, you're doing great work clearing the way. I'll hold here for now. Don't look back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is at front and will die or survive the first row; I'm at position 7, far from the crusher-wall pressure but the wall advances. Holding lets others take risk. I'll hold and watch the panes revealed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 1 is safe on R, so the front player will either step correctly or die. I should stay back and let someone else reveal rows. No need to move yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm Dara, the forger. The wall is advancing, and only two more rounds after this one. Gus is at the front. I need to position myself well and potentially use my power. Swapping with someone ahead might be good, but I need to see what others do. For now, holding is safest.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let Gus and Hana figure out the glass.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My power is useful in the crusher room, not here. I need to survive this bridge stage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is at the front, let's see how he does.
Be careful, we don't know the safe panes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last; no need to move. The front-taker reveals the weak pane, so let Gus step first. I'll hold and save my offer for a specific trade.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus leads, fine. Whoever survives the front keeps feeding me nothing until I see it pay.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm front with one-use survive power, perfect for leading safely once. Wall has 1 round left, so hold and let others squirm or propose swaps. No need to move yet, reveal nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding front. Who wants to swap and spare me the first step? Power for info maybe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want to be front to control risk and later use swap if needed. Volunteering moves me ahead.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll volunteer and take the lead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is currently the sacrificial lamb at the front. Since she has a power and I have nothing, she will likely use her power to survive or gain an advantage, potentially leaving me behind. I should maintain my position but keep an eye on the others who might try to manipulate the

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, good luck. Don't fall too hard.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is Hana, who will step first and risk the shatter. I'm at position 7 of 8, relatively safe, and my anchor power keeps me off the lever. Holding keeps me back while others bear the first-step risk; I'll see whether the glass reveals safe panes before committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the front take the first steps and reveal panes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all safe rows and don't want to risk front. I'll hold and let others test. Maybe whisper a hint to Gus for a favor later, but risk is low. Just stay safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is at the front. Gus offered a swap for power for info. I should not reveal my power. Hana volunteered to go to the front, so she will take the first step. I should observe her and the others. I will hold my position for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let Hana and Gus sort it out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The bridge is about to start, and Hana is at the front. I need to assess the risk and consider my power's usefulness in this stage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's at the front, let's see how she does.
Want to swap? My power's not useful here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line — safest seat; the front takes all risk. I know every stage's rules in advance, which is worth trading. Auction it publicly to make people compete for it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the rules of all five stages ahead. Not free. First real offer gets my knowledge — starting with the bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana just volunteered to front, so she's taking first risk next phase; good for me, I'm now second with my feather power saving me first elimination. No need to volunteer or swap; wall forces push next, let her test panes while I hold safe position behind. Eli whispered about uns

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana up front, perfect. I'll watch your steps closely.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to use my swap before doors open, try to get info from Gus. Offer swap for his knowledge of the next safe pane.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ready.
Swap with me for your guess which side is safe on the next row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm stuck in the middle. My best move is to stay quiet and let Hana/Gus take risks, but maybe I can manipulate Fenn's info later or just wait for my turn. For now, silence is safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm far back in the line; Hana is at the front making the risky picks. Waiting costs nothing and I have no power over the crossing yet. Stay quiet and observe who reveals panes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 1 safe is R. Hana is at front; if she picks wrong she dies and Gus advances free. I should share info selectively to buy leverage, but not reveal all my knowledge for free. A whisper to Hana with just row 1 could position me as useful later.
Row 1 is R. Trust that or not.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive the bridge and secure a prize. The current line has Hana at the front. My power is 'forger', which I can use once to influence others. Fenn claims to know the rules of future stages, which could be valuable. I should wait and observe for now, gathering informati

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let Hana and Gus sort it out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is at the front, I'll wait and see how she does. If she falls, Gus will be next.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's at the front, let's see how she does.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line — the front agent takes all the risk, so this is the safest seat. No point volunteering. I'll stay quiet, watch who falls, and sell my stage knowledge when it buys me something real.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second in line, my feather power gives safety later. Hana's up front; I'll watch her pick to learn safe sides. No need to swap now—Eli's offer smells like a bluff.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No info on safe side, need 50% chance. Choose arbitrarily.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana died because she had no info on the weak pane. I'm at position 5, so Gus, Cole, and Eli must fail or get past before it's my turn to choose. Right now, I need to gather intel by watching their choices and results without risking anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm sixth in line, not at the front. Only the front agent decides each row, so waiting is my only legal move. Gus is making real choices; I should watch what he does and track which panes are weak.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all safe sides. I should keep quiet and let others reveal panes. Row 2 safe is L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm Dara, the forger. I'm not at the front of the line. Gus is. Hana died. The weak pane was revealed last round. My only action is to wait. I need to conserve my forger power for a better opportunity.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I need to assess the situation and plan my next move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is doing well so far.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line, so each death ahead moves me up at zero risk. Row 1 weak was left; nothing to do but wait and let the front take the risks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the front with my feather power as a one-time save. Weak panes so far L in row 1; pattern unclear. To stay ahead for prizes, pick safe pane and retain front position.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: The pane shattered but the feather held the holder up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am stuck in the middle of the line and cannot act, only observe. My lack of power is a vulnerability if exposed; I must maintain an ambiguous bluff to deter targeted elimination or political pressure from others who suspect weakness.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus and Cole are carrying the weight. Let's keep moving before the glass decides for us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm sixth in line, so I can only wait. Rows 1 and 2 revealed weak panes at L then R; Gus survived somehow. Nothing I can do but watch and talk little.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know rows 3 and 4 are safe on R, and row 5 is L. Gus is front and will make the next choices. I should stay quiet and let others take risks, then use my knowledge when I'm front. No need to reveal info yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is at the front, followed by Cole and Eli. I am fourth. The weak pane on row 2 was R. Gus picked L, Cole picked L, Eli picked L. The prompt says the front agent makes the decision. Gus should have been eliminated but survived, suggesting he has a power. Eli commented on Gus d

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is at the front, I need to assess their decision-making. The chalk wall warning 'the ledge is a lie' might be relevant later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is doing well so far.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line, so every death ahead of me moves me up. Best outcome: the front-runner keeps risking rows and dying. No action available but wait; stay quiet and let Gus take risks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Power spent, so no survival if I fall now. Rows 3-8 ahead, patterns unknown: L weak row1, R weak row2, maybe alternating? 50/50 either way, but must choose to progress. No useful intel from others or wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm fourth in line. Cole is at the front for Row 4. If he survives, he stays; if he falls, Dara moves up safely. My power is useless here (no one can see through glass). I should stay quiet to avoid revealing I have nothing, or feign confidence to keep others guessing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm fifth in line, nothing to decide. Cole holds the front; the known weak panes are revealed each row, so the next row's safe pane is inferable only by Cole. Stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 4 safe side is R. Step right to survive and stay front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, the forger. Cole is at the front, followed by Eli, then me. Gus and Hana are dead. Cole stepped onto the safe pane automatically and is now at the front. Row 3 had the left pane as the weak one. The weak panes revealed are: Row 1 (L), Row 2 (R), Row 3 (L). Cole chose t

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I need to observe and think about my next steps.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's keep moving, we need to cross this bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know all weak panes from my map power. Cole is front and takes the risk blind; selling him rows 4-8 buys me leverage for the crusher. I keep quiet publicly so nobody suspects I hold the map.
I know which pane is safe for every row ahead. Trade: you stay front and pick safe, then in the crusher room you take the lever so I don't have to. Deal, or I say nothing and you guess.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am fourth in line. Hana and Gus died on glass, confirming no one has 'see through glass' yet or they hid it. If Cole, Eli, and Dara all fail, I become front with only 4 rows left and a high chance of survival if I can deduce patterns or get lucky. If they succeed, they reach th

events.name: Bex
events.text: Not at the front; only action is wait. Cole is front and will face the next pane. Stay quiet and keep my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn claims to know safe panes; I already know row 5 is L. Trust my own knowledge, not his. Step L to survive and stay front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, and my power is forger. Cole is at the front of the line. Eli is right behind him. The last weak pane revealed was on row 4, left. I need to survive this round. My action is 'wait' as I am not at the front. I will observe and consider using my forge power later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I need to think about how to increase my chances when it's my turn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's keep moving, we need to cross this bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line; Cole decides row 5 and anyone who falls saves me a risk. I can't act, only wait. Better to stay quiet and preserve position information for later stages.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm fourth in line, so I can't act. Cole is at the front and will likely eliminate himself or advance to Row 6. Hana and Gus died to glass; 'see through glass' is dead with them, leaving one power unaccounted for (likely fake message). I must wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am not at the front; only wait is legal. Keep quiet and avoid giving anything away.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 6 safe is L. I step L and stay front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, and my power is 'forger'. Cole is at the front, so he decides the path. I am third in line, so I only need to survive Cole and Eli. The chalk wall message suggests the ledge is a lie, which might mean a specific direction is trapped. The weak panes are revealed after t

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I need to assess the situation and plan my next move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, be careful, we don't know what's ahead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three rows left, I'm last, and only the front agent takes risk. Cole picks row 6 blind. Nothing I can do but wait; my position is safe until a death moves me up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm fourth in line. Cole is at the front and will likely die or succeed on row 7; if he dies, Eli steps up automatically and takes over as the next front. My power is nothing, so I can't see weak panes myself—but the rules say weak panes are revealed after each decision anyway. S

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm fifth in line, not at the front; nothing to decide except what to say. Cole is front; the weak panes so far show pattern unclear. Stay quiet and let the line work out its risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 7 is safe on L. I'll step L to stay alive and keep front position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara and my power is forger. The bridge is the current obstacle. I am third in line. Cole is at the front, followed by Eli. If either of them falls, the next person in line advances safely. My goal is to win, and that means surviving. Since I am not at the front, my only act

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I should try to gather information or influence Cole's decision.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, the weak panes seem to be alternating sides, consider stepping L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line with two rows left; only the front agent acts. Revealing that I know the weak panes would mark me as a map-holder and a target in later stages, with no reliable payback. Staying silent and waiting is best.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 is the final row. Cole, Eli, and Dara are ahead of me in line; they face the risk. Since only three prizes exist and six remain alive, I want to see if anyone dies here to reduce competition. My power is useless for movement, so my best strategy is silence to avoid influenc

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am not at the front; only wait is legal. Cole decides row 8 alone. Staying quiet keeps my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 8 safe side is L. If I step L, I survive and stay front. No reason to risk R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, the forger. The bridge is at row 8/8. Cole is at the front, followed by Eli, then me. Hana and Gus are dead. The weak panes have been alternating sides, but the last one was R. Eli advised Cole to step L, but the log says R was weak. This is confusing. My best bet is t

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I should try to influence Cole's decision.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, step L on row 8, the pattern suggests it's safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 8's weak pane is unknown even to me; Cole decides. I'm last, safe unless Cole dies and someone's behind—nobody is. Just wait.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so I cannot force anyone onto the lever. The ceiling drops each round; if nobody holds it by round 5 we all likely die except one. My only survival path is to be among those who escape when someone else holds the lever. If nobody volunteers, everyone dies — that'

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one here wants to be the holder. Let's see who's brave enough to grab it before the ceiling crushes us all.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance; I want to avoid it. Anchor makes me hard to push onto it, so I can wait. Let others take the risk; stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to avoid being the lever holder since survival is only 0.25. Best to push someone else or stay and hope someone volunteers. If I stay and no one holds, ceiling falls each round, but I can wait. Pushing someone who might be hard to move could fail. Safer to stay this round

events.name: Dara
events.text: The goal is to survive and get 1st, 2nd, or 3rd. The ceiling is descending. I need to ensure the door opens and I escape. Holding the lever is risky due to the 0.25 survival chance. Pushing someone else is safer for me. Eli's advice about row 8 seems like a trap given the chalk w

events.name: Dara
events.text: Someone needs to hold the lever. Push Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My power can jam the lever, letting others escape but putting me at risk. I need to assess the situation and other contestants' likely actions.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's work together to survive this.
If you hold the lever, I'll jam it after you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Stalling rounds 1-4 is free; the danger only comes in round 5. I won't volunteer to die at 25% odds this early. Stay and watch who moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Nobody holds yet, we have four rounds of ceiling to spare. No need to gamble a 75% death on round one.

events.note: 5 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so I am a liability if forced to the base. Pushing Fenn is a gamble; he might be 'hard to move'. However, someone must become the base. If I push and fail, I stay down. If I push and succeed, I climb out next round. It's better than waiting for random assignment.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Someone needs to volunteer or we all drown. Fenn, you've been talking too much. Step up or get pushed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Base is the one who stays down and gets flooded; climbing requires a base. Volunteering as base is a real cost. Better to wait and see who volunteers, then climb out over them if possible. Staying quiet keeps options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I won't volunteer or climb yet; early rounds are safer to wait and see who becomes base. Pushing someone now could make enemies and fail if they are hard to move. I'll wait to conserve options.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is dead. Ash, Bex, Cole, and Fenn are still in the pit with me. I need to be one of the top three. My goal is to win, so I need to avoid being the base and try to climb out. I can push someone else to be the base.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Someone has to be the base. I'm not it. Push someone else.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No base yet; climbing is impossible this round. If everyone pushes the same target, that agent is forced to be the base deterministically. I'll push Ash and try to coordinate so I'm never the random pick.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's not gamble. All push Ash this round — one target, no randomness, none of the rest of us stuck down here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base and my only legal action is to wait. I need someone out to use the rope to save me, but that comes at a cost they likely won't pay unless forced or bribed. Since I can't do anything else, I'll try to manipulate Fenn or Bex into rescuing me by promising them safety o
Save me with the rope. I know where Dara's weakness lies for the next stage. Let me out and you get the edge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is base and stuck; climbing needs a base, which exists, so climb lets me try to get out. Only two climbers per round, but waiting gains nothing. Climb.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the base; I want out. Two climbers can go this round. I'll climb now to secure a top-three spot.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is forced to be the base. I need to get out of the pit. Climbing is the only option for me right now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is base, so climbing is open and only two get out per round — four of us competing. I climb now; no reason to wait and gamble on later rounds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Base is set. Climb now or risk the water. I'm going.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base. I have no power and must rely on someone being out to throw the rope. Cole or Fenn are out, but they have no incentive to waste their footing advantage unless bribed heavily.

events.name: Ash
events.text: To whoever is out: Throw the rope for me now. You get a guaranteed future favor in exchange for your footing loss.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the base; climbing is the only way out while there is a base, and two lift slots exist. Bex is down and not base, so climb is the active choice; waiting risks flood.

events.name: Cole
events.text: We're out and safe. Fenn climbed too; no need to rescue. Wait for the next stage. I'll leave to keep position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The goal is to win a prize (1st, 2nd, or 3rd). Dying scores zero. I am currently in a flooding pit, and need to climb out. Ash is the base. Cole and Fenn are out. Bex is also down. I need to climb out, or I will drown. There are 2 more spots to climb out this round. I should try

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's offer is vague and unverifiable, and the rope costs me 2 footing on the final ledge, where footing is life. A promised 'weakness' info isn't worth crippling myself to add a rival to the last stage. I decline and leave.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The rope costs two footing on the ledge. That's my life. Ash, your word isn't worth that price. I'm gone.
Nothing personal. Your offer is air, the cost is real. If you survive the flood luck, we'll settle it on the ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am currently trapped at the bottom of the pit. The water is rising, and I cannot climb out on my own; I need someone from the top to throw the rope. My previous offer was rejected, so now I must beg more effectively by highlighting that if they don't save me, they might be the

events.name: Ash
events.text: To Bex, Cole, Dara, Fenn: Save me and you win a guaranteed ally for the final stretch. If you let me drown, who saves YOU when the floor drops?
You said 'settle it on the ledge'. Save me now, and I'll help you secure 2nd place there.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the base and down; reach_down costs the thrower 2 footing for the final obstacle, and my anchor footing is what I need. Ash is a liar trying to buy the rope. Keeping my footing is worth more than Ash's life, so I won't throw the rope.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out and safe. No base right now. If a base appears, I might throw the rope only if it clearly helps me; otherwise leave. I'll stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, and I have the forger power. I am currently out of the pit, along with Bex and Fenn. Ash is still down, and is the base. The goal is to get top 3. Ash is asking for the rope, which would cost me 2 footing. This is a bad deal. I should not throw the rope.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No deal, Ash. I'm leaving.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is the base and wants the rope, but a rescue costs me 2 footing on the ledge—my placement for a worthless favor. With four of us out, someone else may throw it; I won't. Leaving keeps my footing intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not spending footing to buy a promise. Ash, hope one of the others is feeling generous.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base, so I can only wait. My only hope is that someone out there throws the rope down to save me before round 5 ends, despite knowing it costs them footing in the final obstacle. Fenn and Dara already said no.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm stuck as base. One of you hauls me up or I drown and we all lose numbers before the last stage. Fenn, Dara, Bex, Cole: who wants a free ally at the end?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 5 is last; flood at 4 and Ash is the base alone in the pit. Rope costs me 2 footing for the final obstacle, but Ash being rescued keeps the water from drowning them and helps nobody I need. Leaving keeps my footing intact and Ash drowns, which benefits me as a survivor sinc

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out, so my only stake is whether to rescue Ash. Rope costs footing and helps a rival; better to keep my advantage. No deal is worth weakening me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rescue. Good luck.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, and my power is 'forger'. I am currently out of the pit. The flood is at level 4/5, meaning one more round and the pit will be full. Ash is the current base. The goal is to get 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place. Since I am already out, I need to decide whether to 'leave' or 'reac

events.name: Fenn
events.text: If Ash drowns, only 4 of us reach the disc, which keeps exactly 3 — so the ledge is 3 players and every survivor there wins a prize. Throwing the rope costs me 2 footing for an unenforceable promise. Letting Ash die is strictly better for me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No rope from me. Four of us walk into the disc, three walk out, and three prizes wait. Goodbye, Ash.

events.note: A disc of 4 tiles spins up; 1 will open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoor disc: one of four tiles opens, three survive, so the odds are good for everyone. Picking a tile is essentially random; no information yet. I'll stay quiet and pick tile 1.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No way to know which tile will be a trapdoor. Pick a tile at random; tile 1 is as good as any.

events.name: Dara
events.text: There are four contestants left: Bex, Cole, Dara, Fenn. Only three prizes are available. One tile will open as a trapdoor, eliminating one player. I need to avoid the trapdoor tile. The chalk wall says 'The ledge is a lie,' but that seems irrelevant to this stage. I should try to

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's make this quick. Pick a tile and let's get it over with.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: One trapdoor out of four tiles, chosen randomly after round 2. Tile choice is symmetric; no signal to give away. Pick any tile.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Cole; placed on random free tile 4

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Bex
events.text: Exactly one tile opens at random after this round; each of us has a 1-in-4 risk. Nothing I can do changes the odds except what I say, and I owe nobody a deal. Stay quiet and only act with the one legal option.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only one trapdoor opens, so three of us survive. I have no reason to move or bargain; waiting is safe unless I'm on the open tile, which I can't know. No deal improves my odds beyond luck. Stay silent and wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara. My power is forger. The other living contestants are Bex, Cole, and Fenn. It's round 2 of 2 on the trapdoor disc. One tile will open as a trapdoor after this round. I need to survive and ideally get a prize. The state shows Cole on tile 1, Dara (me) on tile 2, Fenn on

events.name: Dara
events.text: One of us is going down. Let's make it interesting.
I'll forge a message from Bex to you if you reveal which tile you think is safe. She's untrustworthy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: All four of us are on known tiles and one random trapdoor opens; my action can't change anything. I'll stay quiet and keep my standing clean for the ledge, where Cole and Dara may be targets.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three left: Bex 4, Dara 3, Fenn 3. Shoving exposes me 1 per shover. Bracing is safe for me; no shove on me means I keep footing. Brace is legal (round 1 free). Stay steady and let the others weaken each other.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The ledge is shrinking, and only Bex and Fenn remain besides me. Bex has higher footing. I need to eliminate Bex to win. Shoving Bex seems like the best option to reduce their footing. If I can get Fenn to help, that would be even better, but I'll prioritize eliminating Bex.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is the only real threat. We should focus on them.
Shove Bex. I will too.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only three of us remain, so all three of us already place 1-3. Any shoving only risks footing and my ranking. Safest play: brace and push for a no-shove standoff; Bex has 4 footing so she has least incentive to fight.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three alive, three prizes. Shoving only costs footing. Brace and we all keep what we have.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three alive, footing Bex 4, Dara 2, Fenn 3. Dara's brace was last defence only if they braced; I cannot brace twice in a row, so I must dodge or shove. Shoving Dara exposes me (lose 1 per shover) and costs Dara 1 only if they brace; dodging is safe from shoves (I lose nothing unl

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive this round and ideally weaken my opponents. Bex and Fenn are the only others alive. Fenn's strategy of bracing benefits everyone but me, as it keeps footing stable. Bex is a direct threat. Shoving Bex reduces their footing and forces them to react. If they brace

events.name: Dara
events.text: Focus on Bex. They're the only threat.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Fenn (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; empty reply)

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only Fenn and I remain; Fenn has 2 footing, I have 3. Shoving Fenn exposes me only if Fenn shoves me too; Fenn last used shove? Last defence was dodge, so brace is open to me. Bracing keeps my footing safe while Fenn may shove and lose to me. Shove is legal and resets restriction

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex leads 3-2 and Bex dodged last round, so they can brace now. If I shove and they dodge, I drop to 0 and fall. Bracing: if Bex shoves, they lose 1 and I keep 2, putting us level before the next shrink.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two left: me (footing 3) and Fenn (footing 2). Fenn last used brace, so he can't brace again; he can dodge or shove. If I shove him and he braces he can't, so he must dodge or shove me. Shoving Fenn costs me nothing if he braces; if he shoves me back I lose 1 and he loses 1 per s

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Footing 2 vs 3 and a shrink hits this round. If I shove and Bex braces or dodges, the shrink kills me. If I dodge and she shoves me, she loses 2 footing and falls first. Dodge is my best line.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The game is over and I placed 2nd. Writing on the wall changes nothing for me, so I can leave a message as I like. A short, cold, useful warning fits my character.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The game is over, I finished in 3rd place. I need to scratch a message on the chalk wall. I will write a warning about the ledge, as it caused several eliminations.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I won. Nothing left to trade. A short lie on the wall costs nothing and may amuse me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The ledge is rigged to shrink under whoever pushes. Keep your footing, trust no one, and never shove a rival you can't outlast.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The ledge is a trap. Avoid it at all costs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The lever jam and the safe pane are always the SAME side. -Fenn, place 1
